# Unit Tests

## Gorman Variable Creation

### get_vars_gorman()

The primary barrier is the fact that running variables with an existing feature set is actually slower than running them without one (i.e., it's slower when the `presupplied_variables` argument is filled).

I put the source code of the original below.

```{r, v1-source-code}
get_vars_gorman_og <- function(mode = "book", source, presupplied_variables = NULL) {
  if (mode == "book") {
    # browser()
    source_data <- source |>
      rowwise() |>
      mutate(title = get_title_segment(title))
  } else if (mode == "commentary") {
    source_data <- source |>
      rowwise() |>
      mutate(title = get_title_segment(title, "title"))
  } else if (mode == "chapter") {
    source_data <- source
  } else {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # TOP BRANCH WON'T RUN IN THESE TESTS!!!!
  if (is.null(presupplied_variables)) {
    all_vars <- source_data |>
      group_by(title) %>%
      # lazy_dt() |>
      group_map(~ run_combos(.x, .y, pb = progress_bar$new(total = length(unique(source_data$title))))) |>
      bind_rows() |>
      mutate(title = unlist(title))
  } else {
    
    all_vars <- source_data |>
      # For debugging:
      # slice_sample(n = 100) |>
      rowwise() |>
      # check whether this line is necessary
      # mutate(title = unlist(strsplit(title, "_"))[1:2] |> paste(collapse="_")) |>
      group_by(title) %>%
      group_map(~ count_combinations_per_section_og(presupplied_variables, source_data = .x, title_str = .y)) |>
      bind_rows() |>
      mutate(title = unlist(title)) |>
      unite(col = "pasted", 1:5, sep = "|", na.rm = TRUE)
  }

  return(all_vars)
}

has_all_feature_types_og <- function(row_from_source_data, character_vector_of_feature_values) {
  # Unnecessary when using apply() around this function
  # row_from_source_data %<>% mutate(across(everything(), as.character))

  # if (!is.character(row_from_source_data)) {
  #   row_from_source_data %<>% mutate(across(where(is.factor), as.character))
  # }
  browser()
  # Only return true for this row if ALL characters in the vector on the left are in the row on the right
  # Note on optimization: %chin% is supposedly faster than %in%
  all(character_vector_of_feature_values %in% row_from_source_data)
}

get_number_rows_with_feature_types_og <- function(vector_of_feature_values, source_data) {
  # browser()
  fn_name <- "get_number_rows..."
  
  # Remove X if present
  vector_of_feature_values <- gsub(pattern = "X", replacement = "", vector_of_feature_values)
  
  # Added 9/27/2026: It was detecting the "3" in the title of "philippics_3", 
  #   "gallic_3", etc. as 3rd person, so must remove title
  source_data <- source_data[,colnames(source_data) %notin% c("title", "author", "path", "book", "section")]
  
  count_of_feature_values <- sum(
    apply(X = source_data, MARGIN = 1, FUN = has_all_feature_types_og, character_vector_of_feature_values = vector_of_feature_values)
  )
  log_debug("{fn_name}: The feature values '{paste0(vector_of_feature_values, collapse = ',')}' occurred {count_of_feature_values} times in the dataset.")

  count_of_feature_values
}

count_combinations_per_section_og <- function(combinations, source_data, title_str) {
  # browser()
  t1 <- proc.time()
  norm_val <- 1000 / nrow(source_data)

  # save processing time by converting source_data to matrix now
  source_data <- as.matrix(source_data)

  # more efficient than using rows
  combinations <- t(as.matrix(combinations))

  counts <- apply(combinations, MARGIN = 2, FUN = get_number_rows_with_feature_types, source_data = source_data)
  counts <- counts * norm_val
  return_value <- bind_cols(t(combinations), tibble(n = counts))
  return_value$title <- title_str
  # dplyr::rowwise() %>%
  # summarize(
  #   n = get_number_rows_with_feature_types(c_across(everything()), source_data)
  # ) %>%
  # bind_cols(combinations, .) |>
  # mutate(n = n * norm_val, title = title_str)

  # browser()
  log_info("Finished counting combinations for {title_str}")
  print(proc.time() - t1)
  
  
  return_value
}
```

Any further changes will be documented in commits to the repo on 11/14/2026

First, to load our test_data:

```{r}
source("../functions.R")

# NOTE: REQUIRES HAVING RUN {get-combinations-of-features} CELL IN DATA-PROCESSING.RMD
load("../type_value_pairs.RData")

test_data <- fread("../postagged/postagged-texts.csv", na.strings = "", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = TRUE)

# only care about speed; let's focus on testing Caesar alone for simplicity

test_data %<>% prepare_data()

# Not only subsample, but remove parents
test_data <- test_data[1:1000,1:18]
```
Then to profile it:

```{r}
library(profvis)

profvis::profvis({
  get_vars_gorman(mode = "chapter", source = test_data, presupplied_variables = type_value_pairs)
})
```

It looks like a few places are expensive: the call to `%in%`, the use of `apply()` with `get_number_rows_with_feature_types()`, so I am trying to eliminate that.

My first attempt is to replace `get_number_rows...()` with something more efficient, 
shown in the snippet below:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
get_number_rows_with_feature_types <- function(combination, source_data) {
    combination <- combination[complete.cases(combination)]
    
    indices <- which(source_data %in% combination)
    
    rows <- index_to_row(indices, source_data)
    
    # Keep only rows where the number of cases is equal to the number of features
    #  in the combination
    rows_all <- keep(unique(rows), \(.x) {
      # if a row appears more times than there are cases, that means a single
      #  feature was counted multiple times in one row. That's a problem!
      if (sum(rows == .x) > length(combination)) rlang::abort(
        "Error: one of the features in ({paste0(combination, collapse=',')}) was flagged more than once in row {.x}"
        )
      sum(rows == .x) == length(combination)
      }
    )
    
    length(rows_all)
  }
```

The above makes use of vectorized functions instead of manually looping first by group, then by feature combinations, then by row. Instead of going by row, we can search through the whole matrix

Let's first make sure it doesn't throw an error:

```{r}
get_vars_gorman(mode = "chapter", source = test_data, presupplied_variables = type_value_pairs)
```

What does profvis have to say this time?

```{r}
profvis({
  get_vars_gorman(mode = "chapter", source = test_data, presupplied_variables = type_value_pairs)
})
```
And what about benchmark?

```{r}
bm1 <- bench::mark(
  get_vars_gorman(mode = "chapter", source = test_data, presupplied_variables = type_value_pairs),
  get_vars_gorman_og(mode = "chapter", source = test_data, presupplied_variables = type_value_pairs)
)
```


## Utils

```{r, test-that-index_to_rows}
testthat::test_that("index_to_rows() gets_valid_row", {
  m1 <- as.matrix(penguins)
  for (i in seq(1, 1000)) {
    sampled <- sample(length(m1), 1)
    testthat::expect_lte(index_to_row(sampled, m1), nrow(m1))
    testthat::expect_gt(index_to_row(sampled, m1), 0)
  }
})
```
